week.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers practice naming feelings, noticing cues in faces and bodies, and trying calm-down tools that are safe and child-led. Keep art process-focused—emotion faces should look different on purpose. Use stories and scenarios to build empathy, and protect a cozy calm corner without shame. Strong feelings are welcome; the work is learning helpful next steps together.
week.weeklyMaterials: Emotion cards/posters; shatter-resistant mirrors; feeling puppets; calm-down bottles made with sealed, non-choking fillers (glitter glue sealed shut—no loose beads for mixed-age rooms); paper, crayons, yarn, play dough; comfort corner cushions; scenario picture cards; yoga mats or soft mats; soft music option.
week.teacherPreparation: Stage centers before arrival and preview one open-ended Feelings & Emotions invitation; step back so children lead.
week.familyConnection: We are practicing naming feelings and calm-down strategies at school. Ask at pickup: “What feeling visited you today?” Try a shared belly-breath or a cozy corner at home. There is no perfect feeling—every feeling is okay, and we practice kind next steps.
milestones: Language: Labels common feelings (happy, sad, angry, calm, proud, frustrated) and uses “I feel…” stems.
SEL: Identifies own feelings; notices peers’ cues; practices empathy and calm-down choices without shame.
Cognition: Matches feeling words to faces/scenarios; sequences “what happened / how I felt / what helped.”
Motor: Uses fine motor for dough faces and drawing; participates in yoga/movement with body awareness.
Creativity: Expresses emotions through unique process art and puppet storytelling.

printableIdeas.title: Feelings Face Cards (Large)
printableIdeas.purpose: Printable emotion faces for sorting, check-ins, and charades—children may also draw their own faces so products differ.

printableIdeas.title: Calm Corner Choice Board
printableIdeas.purpose: Picture choices (breathe, squeeze dough, look at bottle, ask for help) posted in the calm corner; ties to real classroom tools.

printableIdeas.title: Feelings Journal Cover (Blank Inside)
printableIdeas.purpose: Optional cover for Feelings Journal Drawing; inside pages stay blank for process drawing—not worksheets with right answers.

songs.title: Feelings Check-In Chant (LLH)
songs.motions: Hands on cheeks for “show a face”; big inhale/exhale on breathe lines; thumbs-up or heart hands on “helpful next step.”
songs.teacherDirections: Open Feelings Circle Check-In. Offer emotion cards so children can point. Validate all answers. Keep chant soft—no performance pressure.
songs.whenToUse: Morning check-in and after conflicts or big transitions.
songs.suggestedPace: Slow and soothing; one verse may be enough.
songs.transitionPurpose: Names feelings and primes calm strategies before centers.
songs.lyrics:
How do you feel? How do you feel?
Show a face, make it real.
Happy, sad, mad, or calm—
Every feeling belongs in our song.

Breathe in slow, breathe out soft,
Feelings come and feelings go.
I can name it, I can choose—
A helpful next step I can use.

songs.title: If You're Happy and You Know It
songs.motions: Match motions to feeling verses; for “mad,” one stomp then hands on belly to breathe—never encourage hitting.
songs.teacherDirections: Extend beyond happy: include mad/sad/calm with safe motions. After mad verse, practice one calm tool together.
songs.whenToUse: Music & movement; Feelings Movement Mirrors warm-up.
songs.suggestedPace: Upbeat for happy; slower for calm verse.
songs.transitionPurpose: Links feeling words to safe body expressions.
songs.lyrics:
If you're happy and you know it, clap your hands.
If you're happy and you know it, clap your hands.
If you're happy and you know it, then your face will surely show it.
If you're happy and you know it, clap your hands.

(Add verses: If you're mad… stomp your feet once then freeze and breathe. If you're calm… hands on heart.)

songs.title: Freeze and Feel (LLH Freeze Dance)
songs.motions: Free dance in personal space; freeze on cue and make a feeling face; resume gently. Offer scarf dancing for children who prefer less facial focus.
songs.teacherDirections: Use soft instrumental or teacher voice only—no copyrighted recorded kids’ songs required. Keep freezes short. Celebrate variety of faces.
songs.transitionPurpose: Releases energy while practicing feeling recognition.
songs.lyrics:
Dance your feelings, move around,
Happy skips or quiet ground.
When I say FREEZE—stop and see:
What feeling face is looking at me?

Soft knees, soft hands, soft feet,
Feelings dance to a gentle beat.
Breathe and smile or breathe and sigh—
Ready, set, feelings fly!

songs.title: Calm Corner Breath Song (LLH)
songs.motions: Cup hands like a flower to “smell”; blow gently; hands on belly for three counts.
songs.teacherDirections: Teach beside the calm corner before Calm Down Bottle Exploration. Practice as a group so the corner feels familiar, not punitive.
songs.whenToUse: Before rest, after big feelings, or as a transition into quiet work.
songs.transitionPurpose: Installs a shared, non-shame calm routine.
songs.lyrics:
Smell the flower, blow the pinwheel slow,
Smell the flower, let the soft air go.
Hands on belly, one, two, three—
Calm is growing inside of me.

teacherToolkit.teacherPreparation: Stage centers before arrival and preview one open-ended Feelings & Emotions invitation; step back so children lead.
prepChecklist: Set materials at child height before arrival
Preview one Feelings & Emotions invitation aloud
Place cleanup caddy near the play space
Review allergy and supervision notes for the day
observationFocus: Uses Feelings & Emotions vocabulary in play
Persists with a material or peer exchange
Shows interest or curiosity during invitations
observationPrompts: What language or gestures appear during play?
How does the child enter and leave the invitation?
Where do peers support or extend the idea?
documentationPrompts: Capture one moment of child-led exploration (with permission).
Note a verbatim quote or gesture tied to the theme.
teacherTips: Model once, then narrate what you notice.
Offer two choices instead of open-ended demands.
Keep transitions short with a familiar song cue.
setupCleanupShortcuts: Trays labeled and stacked by day
Damp cloth + bin for quick reset
Spare substitution basket on the shelf

materialSubstitutions.use: printed picture cards or recycled clean containers

teacherToolkit.mixedAgeAdaptations: Offer a simpler parallel tray for younger friends and a design challenge for older preschoolers.
teacherToolkit.extraSupportAdaptations: Sit beside, shorten the invitation, and offer hand-under-hand only when welcomed.
teacherToolkit.challengeExtensions: Invite children to invent a new Feelings & Emotions rule, map, or story for peers.
teacherToolkit.safetyInclusionNotes: Calm-down tools must not introduce choking hazards: fully seal bottles; avoid loose beads/glitter in mixed-age rooms; offer scarves, dough, pillows, or picture books instead. Process art only—no identical “right” emotion crafts. Never send children to a calm corner as punishment. Mixed-age: keep yarn lengths short, dough out of mouths, and mirrors shatter-resistant. Supervise yoga so children do not push necks/backs. Allergy-check any scented lotions if used for calm tools (prefer unscented).
teacherToolkit.endOfWeekReflection: Which Feelings & Emotions words and strategies showed up most in play?
teacherToolkit.familyConnection: Share one Feelings & Emotions word or song to try at home during ordinary routines.
teacherToolkit.notes: Draft toolkit for owner review — enrichment draft only.

legacySnapshot.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers will explore feelings and emotions through stories, art, movement, discussions, and pretend play. Children will name emotions, recognize feelings in themselves and others, and practice helpful strategies for managing strong feelings.
legacySnapshot.objectives:
Identify and name common emotions
Recognize emotional expressions on faces
Connect feelings to experiences and stories
Practice calming and coping strategies
Build empathy through discussion and role play
Express feelings through art and movement
